reviews.comment: He is honestly really sweet. He would do pop quizzes, but they would show up on canvas, so you would know what days. He does seem like he wants you to learn. Would take him again
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Not a bad option. His lectures were usually pretty dry, but the information was there. He was always willing to answer questions, and he appreciated it when we were curious. Assignments were pretty straightforward, just sometimes annoying. Exams were easy as long as you review slides to study.

Honestly a good prof. He covered material in depth and gave easy exams if you study. I used Gizmo to plug in powerpoints and make practice questions and it helps a lot. He gives extra credit and a good amount of assignments to recover your grade. Definitely a little work but nothing too extreme
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Pretty laid back guy. His lectures were kind of dry sometimes, but you can tell he really prioritizes engagement and discussion. Didn't even have to be directly tied to the topic, I think he just liked hearing us talk and being curious. Occasional pop-quizzes, but the exams were pretty straightforward with some light studying.

Taken Fall 2025. He gave decent extra credit. Attendance was only mandatory on days with quizzes or exams. Exams were straight-forward and matched slides very well. Only hard exam was exam 3, but if you do well on the other 3 you'll be fine. No cumulative final, just another exam. Professor Riviere was passionate and knowledgeable.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory there's a few pop quizzes. For projects he gave us many resources (an example, videos, and very clear instructions) to complete it to the best of our ability. His lectures weren't the most interesting, but they were clear and to the point, so they were easy to understand. Studying the slides as flashcards for tests is good.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This professor is amazing. I don't see why he has a 3.5 rating. His class was easy. There was no textbook, and the tests were straightforward. The projects were easy, and I got 100's on all of them. You do have to go to class because there's pop quizzes and you have to fill in the blanks on the powerpoint, which you can use during the quiz.

Professor Riviere isn't a bad professor, he just makes very bland lectures. The class is very easy, you just have to literally memorize the lectures and you'll do good on the tests. There is a semester long project, but it is extremely easy. The class is easy, I would just not take Riviere again.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He was an OK professor, knowledgeable about nutrition but mostly read off the slides during lecture. Uses campus knot for graded attendance and gives multiple pop quizzes, though they were open note and pretty easy. Overall not bad and decent.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Easy class if you attend. He reads off slides, but attendance is important because slides have blanks filled in during lecture. Tests are basically the slides and the study guide. DAPs take time but boost your grade if done right. Quizzes are easy if you choose the open note pop quiz option. The professor is funny and very straight to the point.

His rating should be higher. HW and quizzes are easy/open-note. Tests are easy and straight from slides. As long as you follow the examples for the DAP, you should be good. Final isn't cumulative. He's funny and lowk sassy. LOTS of extra credit and reviews. He takes attendance, but always lets us out early. God forbid someone reads off the slides.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He read off of slides the entire time so his class was always boring. For me the tests were difficult even though I studied. His project boosts your overall grade but beware of due dates, he will not make it clear.  And be ready for quizzes. Attendance is mandatory. Could be worse, but I don't recommend.

NUTR 202 was super chill because of him. The exams were extremely similar to the test reviews he posts, and the DAP project he gave us over the semester was straight forward and interesting. There are around 5 pop quizzes, but they were open note. He also appreciates participation in class and just wants to help you do good. Great professor overall

He's super nice/chill but doesn't have time for disrespectful students during lecture. Exams are pretty straightforward. Attendance is graded throughout semester. A lot of opportunities for extra credit. Pop quizzes are random, if you attend class every day, pretty easy A. Semester-long project, but it's actually helpful to know/interesting.

Super chill guy and very nice, you can tell he's passionate about nutrition and he loves to answer questions. Treats the class like it's high school and you won't learn much (reads off slides) but it's an easy A. Attendance is mandatory via campus knot and you will have in/out of class participation assignments but they help boost your grade.

Pretty good class. Theres only two hard units for the vitamins and minerals chapter because theres a lot of memorization but overall super easy class. Pop quizzes are open notes though but beware he puts a time limit to 10 minutes for 10 questions so you need to do control f to search the docs on the quizzes or youll run out of time.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is my goat. Easy class just memorize the slides. I never listened to his lectures and got A's on my exams. He is my LeBron. He is my hero. He is what I aspire to be. Not even glaze.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I loved this class! I have always found nutrition interesting and thoroughly enjoyed how he made the lectures comprehensive, but understandable. He was very knowledgeable and able to answer questions students asked in class. He does open note quizzes, and the homework is few and far between. Overall great class and very informative!

Great nutrition intro course! Tests (lockdown browser) are straightforward if you just memorize the slides and listen in class. Full-semester project split into 3 parts that was an easy A. He takes time to cater the lectures to your questions. There were pop-quizzes, but they were open-note, not lockdown, and pretty easy. Take him!
I submitted a project blank and he let me resubmit it for half credit. Lectures are boring but the class isn't hard if you know biology.

I personally liked Professor Riviere. The class is quite easy as long as you show up to lecture. You are graded on very little things. But overall it's a pretty easy course just attention. There are pop quizzes so be prepared and take notes.
reviews.ratingTags: Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: As long as you go to class, it's a pretty easy A. Attendance taken randomly, open note pop quizzes. Show up, learn the slides, do the short assignments and project correctly because it really does boost your grade. Overall, not too difficult class as long as you put in some effort!
he takes attendance
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This was such an easy class, I don't know how people struggled. All content is gone over during lecture, so listen and take notes. Many bonus point opportunities had me sitting at a 110/100 in the class for most of the semester. Become a Quizlet warrior and just learn every detail from the slides and you will make As on the exams. He's a great prof
This professor is not great but he gives so many bonus points and ez quizzes that it doesn't even matter. If you do the assignments and show up to class then it should be an easy A
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: This guy is underrated, tests are free, good amnt of bonus points. Lectures can be very boring, but what ur graded on is so ez it doesnt matter. Make sure to attend lectures as its mandatory and study tests a couple days in advance. Tests are similar to slides so tests were very ez and final isnt even cumulative. Guy gets too much hate on here.

First test was much harder than expected . Watch out for the first DAP grade, dropped my grade. He kicked people out of class for being on their phones in a class of 200, then would take attendance. HE DOES TAKE ATTENDANCE ALMOST EVERY CLASS. Don't bother trying to explain to him why you missed class. I was sick and didn't even bother emailing him.

Professor will randomly assign in-class assignments without any warning and will give pop quizzes. Attendance taken randomly, but often, and for a grade. Lectures can be boring, yet interesting information is covered. Slides are on Canvas, but there are fill-in-the-blanks, so you need to attend lectures to have the full notes. Not a super easy A.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: I became severely ill early in the semester and communicated everything with documentation. When I left class due to extreme pain and emailed Professor Riviere, he blamed me and refused to extend an assignment. I later went to the ER for a kidney infection. He reopened it only after another note, with no apology. I felt disrespected and dismissed.

Prof Riviere is alright if you can't get into another section or course. The content is delivered through lectures that he will change to try and meet student needs. There is random graded attendance and questions through CampusKnot which didn't like to work well for me. The tests are fairly basic as are the pop-quiz. Long semester project!!

Attendance is mandatory as he does random questions, attendance & easy pop quizzes that can only be done in class. He's kind of rude to people and a stickler about rules. He walks around the class, ensuring ppl are doing work, even in a class of 200. Tests are recorded on lockdown, & questions can be unnecessary. The online course is so much easier

Aaron is a good professor. He does read off the power points yes, but its all important information and if you pay attention, take decent notes, and study a couple days before the exam, youll be fine. If you show up in class and participate, you should get a good grade. I made the mistake of missing quite a few classes, thats why I got a B.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is super chill and would let class out early all the time. He releases study guides before the exam that are really similar to the test questions, I would do them the day of and get As. He has an extra credit quiz at the beginning that had my grade at 132% for a while. Class is super chill and easy if you have a brain. I love that man. 10/10

He randomly has iClickers and in-person attendance activities so try to go to class. Always go to class the lecture before the exam, he does review iClickers that are really helpful. He seems like a nice guy, so just try to go to class and study and you'll be okay.

He seems like a decent guy, but like every other review on here he just reads off slides that he probably didn't make himself. I get it is hard to be engaging in a class with 200 people in it, but come on. Strikes me as a guy that's just teaching to get his research done, not there to actually teach you or further your education. Average at best.

He was a pretty boring teacher but it wasn't difficult to be in his class. There were a decent amount of in class assignments and IClickers so you do actually have to show up, he just reads off of the slides and it's kind of boring but you'll live through it. The tests are basically word for word from the slides/test reviews so just study those.

Such an easy class. His lectures were sometimes boring because he just reads off the slides but if you participate and do the in class assignments, you're basically guaranteed to get full credit on them. Exams are literally straight from his slides so just memorize and you'll do perfectly fine
Accidentally submitted a wrong document for an assignment, when I emailed him he didnt care and gave me a 0

Randomly does iclicker, usually let us out early, didn't really need to pay attention to lectures if you study the slides and study guides. Not very enthusiastic. Some homework was a little annoying but not bad, there's a couple random quizzes and assignments in class so go, tests weren't bad if you study.

Reads verbatim off slides, but you can ignore him and I stopped doing notes and just answered the learning objectives. Theres reviews for all the exams. There can be random questions, but you can get a good grade regardless. Pop quizzes that are open note, and the project is easy. Class ends early alot. Whoever says this class is hard is a joke.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: You have to teach yourself everything if you want to do well in this class. He lectures the entire session, reads verbatim off the slides, and I'm 99% sure he does not even make them himself. He often let us out of class an hour early. Tests are straight forward, just cover a lot of information along with small details that are really easy to miss.

He goes super fast through the lectures, basically just reading word-for-word from slides that I don't even think he prepared himself. You have to teach yourself the content for the tests. I will say that the tests are pretty straightforward from the slides, but there's no actual teaching during class.

I loved this class, the information was very interesting. He talked very fast, so I took notes before class over the slides. The exams are straight from the slides. Random attendance taken, but not graded. All assignments/quizzes are pop, so it is important to attend. He drops your lowest 2 assignments and lowest quiz.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's nice and knowledgeable, but he sort of just reads off of the slides, and really quickly too. The time spent in minutes is usually lower than the number of slides, so taking detailed notes in this class is pretty much out of the question. Attendance is technically mandatory but its random as to whether he takes it or not.

His slides are available outside of class, some group assignments and a semester-long project divided into parts. Look out for small details from notes which are often on the test, attendance is taken on iClicker. He's a decent professor and the class isn't hard if you study thoroughly before an exam (grades are exam-heavy). Would recommend!
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things
